newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PM Kok against EU Big Three proposal.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PM Kok against EU Big Three proposal.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Friday he was not in favour of a proposal to cede more power to France, Germany and Britain in European affairs in the interests of faster decision-making.

The EU foreign relations commissioner, Hans van den Broek, said last Saturday the "Big Three" should be given greater influence in return for pledging a more pro-European foreign policy approach and agreeing to more decisions on the basis of qualified majority voting.

"I think the consequence of this suggestion would be that small and medium-sized countries would get the feeling they were being pushed aside," Kok told reporters in The Hague. The Netherlands currently holds the rotating EU presidency.
Under Van den Broek's proposal, made only in a personal capacity, smaller member states would lose the right to veto EU decisions.
Paris, Bonn or London would only be able to block decisions through a joint veto involving at least two of them.
